dedupe_keys.name: agent based simulation outputs of urban emergency vehicle response in barcelona s eixample netlogo reproducibility package

description: This package holds the outputs of a simulation that asks how much traffic lights and rush-hour congestion slow an emergency vehicle crossing central Barcelona. The producers are Antonio González Cuevas, Álvaro Wong González and Remo Suppi Boldrito, who built an agent-based model in NetLogo linked to street maps for their paper on urban emergency response. Coverage is a 1,250 metre corridor in the Eixample district, run 30 times under each of three scenarios: free-flowing streets, four active traffic signals, and signals with calibrated morning-peak traffic of about 24,660 vehicles. Mean response times rose from 124.5 seconds to 144.5 seconds with signals and 201.3 seconds with congestion, so congestion added almost three times the delay of signals. The deposit gives run-level results, the traffic calibration files, corridor metadata and a data dictionary, available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: one short corridor, simulated, not observed trips, and the deposit centres on outputs and calibration files, not a packaged model. Simulation uses: validating emergency vehicle routing and signal pre-emption models, and estimating how congestion changes ambulance and fire response times. Related records: MATSim (model-matsim) simulates city traffic, and the San Francisco fire and EMS calls (data-sf-fire-ems-calls-for-service) give observed response times.
